Hi Priya — technical detail from the platform side (long but explicit so Legal can rely on it):

1) Serving locality (region pinning)
- Production inference and stored request/response artifacts for your tenant will be served and written only in us-west-2. Our scheduler and data-plane routing enforce per-tenant region affinity for Dedicated pools; requests will not be routed to other regions except for manual emergency failover (see DR notes) or if you explicitly enable multi-region.

2) Backups & snapshots
- Nightly snapshots of model KV caches and persistent tenant metadata are created in us-west-2. By default, snapshots are also replicated to a single DR region (us-east-1) to satisfy platform recovery SLAs.
- Replicated snapshots are encrypted with a different envelope key (customer tenant key + region salt) and stored in a separate bucket with MFK (multi-key fragmentation) separation. Access to DR copies is restricted to the recovery runbook and requires two-person ops authorization.
- Important: replication to DR can be disabled on the contract for customers with strict in-country-only requirements. If you require zero cross-region snapshot replication, we will disable scheduled DR replication and instead maintain an in-region cold-snapshot store with the same retention period.

3) Deletion and teardown workflow
- Step 1: Initiate tenant teardown (customer-initiated or contract termination) — we mark all metadata and index pointers as tombstoned and remove serving routing within minutes.
- Step 2: Logical deletion pass — keys referencing object storage are removed and databases are scrubbed of PII over the next 72 hours.
- Step 3: Snapshot purge schedule — snapshots and backups are queued for deletion; if DR replication was enabled, we trigger deletion in the DR region as well. Snapshot purging completes within 30 days by default.
- Step 4: Physical expunge and overwrite — object storage lifecycle ensures final physical overwrite or vendor-specified secure deletion within 90 days from teardown request.

We can tighten this timeline in the SOW: e.g., 14-day snapshot purge + 45-day physical expunge with a contractual audit right.

4) Legal holds
- Legal holds: we support suspending deletion workflows for up to 12 months by default while preserving audit trails. Extending beyond 12 months is possible via written agreement (we’ll maintain isolated retention but it counts against storage commitments).

Auditability & evidence
- For each step we record audit logs, deletion job run IDs, and storage object manifests. We can provide a signed attestation and a manifest showing object ids and deletion job timestamps when you request a teardown.

Operational constraints & notes
- If you opt-out of DR replication, your recovery RTO increases and we will include that in the SOW.
- Keys: if you bring your own key (BYOK via KMS), we can limit key escrow so that we cannot decrypt DR copies without your cooperation — gives you stronger guarantees for cross-region data access.

I’ve attached a one-page commitment for Legal and flagged the clauses we recommend tightening in the SOW. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk Legal through the steps.

Regards,

Hi Priya and team — appreciate the quick review. Summary and commitments we can include in the MSA / SOW: 

1) Region pinning: Redwood confirms that serving and tenant-scoped stored artifacts will be pinned to us-west-2 for the Dedicated cluster, unless LumenPay requests multi-region enablement in writing.

2) Snapshot replication: Redwood will disable automated cross-region snapshot replication for LumenPay if requested. When disabled, no scheduled snapshots will be copied to other regions; emergency manual copies require written approval and two-person ops authorization and will be logged and reported.

3) Deletion windows: Redwood accepts the following contractual windows: logical deletion completed within 30 days, final physical expunge completed within 90 days. We will deliver a signed deletion manifest within 10 business days of the final expunge.

4) Legal holds: Redwood can pause deletion workflows for up to 12 months upon valid written request; extensions are available via written agreement.
